task_commit_basis: merge commit of the reference change (code after the optimization landed), from https://github.com/scipy/scipy/commit/ce1f46f895c4e06f4aafcd0bb43f84f93b81cc3a

reference_change.title: ENH: linalg.cholesky: leverage symmetry for performance

workload.command: python -c "import numpy as np; from scipy.linalg import cholesky; a = np.random.default_rng(0).random((512, 512)); a = a @ a.T + 512 * np.eye(512); [cholesky(a, lower=False) for _ in range(300)]"
workload.source: written here from the description of https://github.com/scipy/scipy/pull/24913 (real 512x512 matrices with lower=False, the case its regression hit hardest): repeated scipy.linalg.cholesky on a fixed positive-definite matrix

oracle.source: scipy's Cholesky tests (scipy/linalg/tests/test_decomp_cholesky.py, which https://github.com/scipy/scipy/pull/24913 extends); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 3x; 5x | timings: 0.016ms; 0.018ms; 0.009ms; 0.047ms; 0.063ms; 0.024ms; 0.106ms; 0.153ms | benchmark files changed: benchmarks/benchmarks/linalg.py

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. Built from source with meson-python against Apple Accelerate and without Fortran (no Fortran compiler here; scipy's _without-fortran option), git submodules fetched at their pinned commits. Python and dependencies are pinned to the change's era (see eval/README.md, Built and run here)
